newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council urges Croatia to treat Serbs better.
newsitem.headline: UN Council urges Croatia to treat Serbs better.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council on Wednesday again criticised Croatia for failing to protect Serb citizens, despite improvement in their living conditions.

The council, at a formal meeting, based its statement on a recent report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan who said Zagreb had made little progress in its treatment of minority Serbs over the last three months.
Expressing deep concern, the council "called on Croatia to take further steps to restore a climate of law and order" in areas Serbs had dominated until Croatia's 1995 military offensive.
It said Croaitan Serbs continued to "live in conditions of serious insecurity."

Up to 200,000 Serbs fled when Zagreb's troops recaptured the Serb-dominated Krajina region in two swift offensives in mid-1995. Only a few Serbs remained in the area and about 14,000 have been allowed to return.

The council said there was little progress in facilitiing the return of Croatia Serbs who had fled or been driven out during the offensive and Croatia should "remove bureaucratic obstacles" in issuing them documents.

It also called on Croatia to "remove uncertainty" in implementing an amnesty law by publicising the names of people it suspected of war crimes. It said Zagreb should "put an end to arbitrary arrests particularly of Serbs returning to Croatia."

The council said Croatia withheld full cooperation with the Hague-based tribunal on the former Yugoslavia. The U.N. tribunal has indicted some 74 suspects -- 53 Serbs, 18 Croats and three Moslems. But most remain at large.
The Security Council reviews Croatia's human rights situation about every three months, a process the Zagreb government says singles it out unfairly.
